placement.rows_unit: One valid source row traversing six logical expert slots in one layer.

contracts.source: Existing six BF16 expert vectors return to source rank. Match original full-precision product and addition order and final BF16 rounding.
contracts.local_choice: Per-source row minimizes cross-card operand + final vectors, then all inter-rank vectors, then prefers source. Rank ID breaks ties. Includes a direct source-to-expert route decision; row capacity is measured, not enforced.
contracts.capped: Card-only optimal dual prices on the same routes; construct capacity-feasible token/card choices by moving along eligible ties. For fixed cards choose the two chip counts to minimize inter-rank exchanges subject to original peak rank-row cap. Each of 160 scalar costs must match independently saved dual optimum. Global optimum for sibling traffic is unknown.
contracts.idle_partner: Fixed other-DP partner rank XOR 8, same padded row position. Move only on positive inter-card saving and if the counterpart position is inactive. Holds at most original maximum M rows per chip on all observed routes. Requires peer active-mask knowledge or exact equivalent length contract.
contracts.prefix: At least three consecutive slots from slot zero on the same remote chip (or card). Compute their original-order FP32 prefix; return FP32 if more slots follow or final BF16 if all six. All later slots return directly to original source. Card calculation may need sibling transfers. Source retains the final result. No regrouping of a suffix or change in rounding.

limits: Logical BF16 vectors omit link protocol and HBM implementation. A one-way volume or peak is not a duration or guaranteed acceleration.
Two serial cross-card legs refer to an expert operand entering a remote reducer before its final BF16 result can return to source. Scalar weights and route metadata are additional dependencies.
Per-layer peak counters are directional and independent. Do not add send, receive or rank/card maxima into a critical path.
Existing pinned kernel uses cross-rank synchronization before weighted unpermute. Moving the reducer requires a publication/ready rule for the returned final vector.

one_crossing.argument: With the exact linear FP32 accumulator, a remote accumulator must visit the source to deliver the result. To allow at most one off-card edge along any expert-result path, every operand consumed at the remote site must originate on its card, and no second remote site may follow. Only an original consecutive prefix can be computed there. Return its FP32 state or, after all 6 slots, final BF16. Once at source, remaining operands arrive directly. Applies only to whole-width vectors, fixed expert placement and this arithmetic chain; control/weights are outside this depth bound.

implementation_tradeoff.scope: One-off scalar route control is additional to the tensor edges. Ratio assumes aggregate serial payload time only. The local staging term is a scenario; direct peer write to the final destination can avoid that copy subject to correct readiness.

observed_readers.first_identified_numeric_routed_consumer: ForeachAddList shared BF16 + routed BF16 at original query-row shard, followed by HcPost. FusedMC2 selects MC2 prepare/finalize. The shared expert reads its own input. Earlier INT32 and mask work is not a numerical consumer of the BF16 routed matrix.
observed_readers.stream_relation: All intervening recorded typed native tasks and the add are on the same stream as F21. No archived collective overlaps F21 end to merge start in these 2560 brackets. No time here is an automatic overlap credit. Views, counters and unrecorded operations retain their contracts.

conditional_rate.conditions: Different recordings with identical M, layer, rank and all 16 valid source-row counts. Divide candidate cross-card final bytes to each destination rank by its own archived F21 exit to merge interval. Also show the interval excluding observer/other work, retaining just four shared task durations. Assume result ready at the old exit, an independent transport stream, unchanged merge deadline and no contention. Earlier/later tile readiness changes the calculation. Maximum of 16 destination rates per call; neither observed bandwidth, guaranteed slack nor a model speedup.

relations.prefix_and_whole_row: Alternative placements of the same six slots; do not add bytes. The capped whole-row policy requires the extra dependent final hop on nearly every cross-card relocation. The one-crossing proof does not cover reassigning experts, changing numeric semantics or moving the final user.
relations.expert_and_reducer_placement: Current numbers use stock expert owners. Accepted load balancing would change which original slot results are remote; the guarded sparse layout already has a distinct capped-card saving of 5.648 GB. Reprice the joint placement once using its own coordinates.
relations.shared_merge_and_HC: If the routed result stays at the new owner, the BF16 shared result and required original residual/coefficients or final four residual planes must move or be computed there. Count these edges and respect SP and shared-present/absent branches before removing the final return.
relations.small_shapes_and_unseen_paths: This natural prefill result does not resolve graph decode, draft, unobserved shape branches, or a different quantization/numeric order.

reader_and_depth.decision: Defer a standalone one-crossing prefix implementation on this route census; reopen only for a demonstrated critical concentration or a shared producer that removes more work. The full capped two-leg protocol still merits one calibration that isolates true remote BF16 epilogue placement and prices final delivery/ready barriers. Keep numeric equivalence and full operator time separate.
